title: AIMER: Calibration-Free Task-Agnostic MoE Expert Pruning
abstract: arXiv:2603.18492v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models increase parameter capacity without proportional per-token computation, yet deployment still requires storing the full expert pool, making expert pruning important for reducing memory and serving overhead. Existing task-agnostic expert-pruning methods are typically calibration-dependent: they estimate expert importance from routing or activation statistics on a calibration set, making pruning decisions sensitive to calibration-data variation while introducing substantial preprocessing cost. We propose AIMER (\textbf{A}bsolute mean over root mean square \textbf{IM}portance for \textbf{E}xpert \textbf{R}anking), a simple calibration-free criterion that identifies more distinct experts by capturing the concentration pattern of expert weights, making it well suited for task-agnostic expert pruning. translated_title: AIMER：无需校准的任务无关MoE专家剪枝方法
translated_abstract: 混合专家模型在增加参数容量的同时无需按比例增加每个token的计算量，但部署时仍需存储完整的专家池，因此专家剪枝对于降低内存和服务开销非常重要。现有的任务无关专家剪枝方法通常依赖校准数据：它们在校准集上基于路由或激活统计信息来估计专家重要性，这使得剪枝决策对校准数据的变化较为敏感，同时引入了大量预处理成本。我们提出了AIMER（基于均方根之上的绝对平均值专家排序重要性），这是一种简单的无需校准的准则，通过捕捉专家权重的集中模式来识别更具独特性的专家，使其非常适合任务无关的专家剪枝。在具有不同架构的7B至47B MoE语言模型以及16个多样化基准测试上，AIMER……
tldr: 提出了AIMER，一种无需校准数据的MoE专家剪枝准则，通过专家权重的集中模式对专家重要性进行排序，实现任务无关的高效剪枝。
en_tdlr: AIMER is a calibration-free criterion for task-agnostic MoE expert pruning that ranks expert importance by capturing the concentration pattern of expert weights.
